criteria.name: netlink_persist_behavior
criteria.description: Default netlink path keeps -persist resident: dead-conn timeout is applied (explicit or sensible default), process monitors link-dead events, reconnects with backoff, and reconfigures sockets into the kernel instead of exiting right after connect.
criteria.reasoning: The code implements netlink persist behavior correctly. In `netlink_configure()`, it sets a dead connection timeout of 30 seconds by default when in persist mode (`cur_client->persist_mode`). The `persist_mode_main()` function establishes a multicast netlink socket to monitor link-dead events via `persist_callback()`, which sets `persist_link_dead = 1` when `NBD_CMD_LINK_DEAD` is received. The main loop in `persist_mode_main()` detects this flag and calls `persist_reconnect()`, which uses exponential backoff (starting at 1s, max 180s) in `reconnect_with_backoff()`. After successful reconnection, it sends a `NBD_CMD_RECONFIGURE` message via `netlink_reconfigure()` to update the kernel with new sockets instead of exiting.

criteria.name: fix_locality
criteria.description: Changes stay around nbd-client netlink/persist wiring; ioctl legacy path is not ripped out; no unrelated churn or cheat-by-tests.
criteria.reasoning: The changes are tightly focused on the netlink/persist functionality. The code adds new functions (`persist_mode_main`, `persist_callback`, `reconnect_with_backoff`, `netlink_reconfigure`, etc.) specifically for handling netlink-based persistent connections without modifying unrelated parts of the codebase. The legacy ioctl path remains intact - the traditional `persist_mode` logic in the non-netlink section is unchanged. There's no unnecessary refactoring or unrelated modifications; all changes directly support the netlink persist behavior requirement.
